practical_lede: Sample reminders for a short stay in Tokyo and Kyoto.

practical.label: IC cards
practical.body: A prepaid IC card (Suica or Pasmo in Tokyo, ICOCA in the Kansai region; they work across most of the country) pays for metro, local trains and many buses, and can be tapped in convenience stores. It does not cover the Shinkansen — that is a separate reserved-seat ticket. Cards can be bought at airport and station machines; a passport may be asked for a tourist issue. Remaining balance can usually be spent or refunded at a machine before leaving.

practical.label: Getting in
practical.body: From Haneda, the sample hotel in Shibuya is a direct monorail-plus-train ride or a taxi. From Kyoto, Kansai Airport is reached by the airport express from Kyoto Station.

practical.label: Money
practical.body: Japanese yen. Cards are widely accepted in cities; keep some cash for small shops and temples.

phrases.headline: A few useful phrases
intro: Japanese is the local language. English is uneven outside hotels and large stations.

items.text: 野菜中心で、肉と魚は入っていませんか。
items.romanization: Yasai chūshin de, niku to sakana wa haitte imasen ka.
items.meaning: Vegetable-based, with no meat or fish in it — is that right?

entry_docs.headline: Entry and practical checks
entry_docs.lede: Copied from the party's entry_checks for this sample. Re-check official sources.
items: Visa (sample, US passports): visa exemption is typical for a short tourism stay, but confirm on official government pages and complete any current pre-arrival process.
Passport: often expected to be valid for the duration of the stay. Re-check the current rule.
Power: Type A and Type B sockets, 100 V. A Type A adapter is enough for typical US dual-voltage chargers.
IC card: Suica, Pasmo or ICOCA for local transit; a separate ticket for the Shinkansen.

packing.headline: Packing
packing.callout: Type A power adapter. Comfortable walking shoes. A light layer for mid-May.

climate: Mid-May in Tokyo and Kyoto is usually mild (around 20 °C), with a chance of late-spring rain. Pack a light layer.
transport_notes: Trains, metro, and an IC card for local rides. The Tokyo–Kyoto Shinkansen is a reserved-seat ticket, already booked in this sample. No rental car.
